project.title: Multi-Account Build of the Cloud Services Directorate (CSD) Landing Zone
project.role: AWS Cloud Infrastructure as Code DevOps Engineer & Architect

parentsummary.deliverables: Led the design and delivery of the CSD Landing Zone—a codified multi-account AWS foundation built first on AWS Landing Zone and then on ASEA—deployed through a CodePipeline, CodeBuild, and GitLab pipeline.
parentsummary.outcomes: Adopted as SSC's standard AWS landing zone, onboarding 3 early adopter workload clients and completing landing zone upgrades in about 4 hours including testing and validation.

challenge.summary: Shared Services Canada (SSC) teams previously operated AWS workloads in stand-alone or loosely coupled accounts, with no shared standard or central control across the department and often none between projects in the same directorate. Standing up a net-new Cloud Services Directorate (CSD) Landing Zone spanned two platform iterations—starting on AWS Landing Zone before moving to the AWS Secure Environment Accelerator (ASEA)—while in-house Government of Canada expertise centred on on-premises data-centre models that did not translate directly to hyperscale cloud. Without a unified multi-account foundation, SSC had no consistent security, governance, or financial accountability over its AWS platforms.

deliverables: Designed the CSD Landing Zone multi-account structure using AWS Organizations and core accounts, with Core, Maintenance, Quarantine, and Custom organizational units (OUs) plus workload profile OUs each divided into production (Prod) and non-production (NonProd)
Built the first landing zone iteration on AWS Landing Zone and the second on ASEA with its Security Guard Rails, working in close partnership with the AWS Canada ASEA team
Configured ASEA Security Guard Rails to meet the Treasury Board of Canada Secretariat (TBS) cloud guardrails
Codified the AWS Landing Zone and ASEA configuration, including organization-specific custom code, stored in GitLab and AWS CodeCommit
Built the CI/CD deployment pipeline for the landing zone using AWS CodePipeline, AWS CodeBuild, and GitLab

Collaborated on and contributed to the cloud network design across Virtual Private Cloud (VPC), AWS Transit Gateway, and Virtual Private Network (VPN) connectivity for traffic entering and leaving the cloud (north-south) and moving between networks (east-west), and supported the design and integration of FortiGate next-generation firewall appliances
Produced documentation and ran knowledge transfer for the team, new staff, and onboarded clients

outcomes: 3 early adopter workload clients were onboarded onto the CSD Landing Zone
Landing zone upgrades completed in about 4 hours, including testing and validation
The platform became SSC's standard AWS landing zone, later iterated on by the AWS ASEA team, SSC teams, and other government departments
